newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says Taipei envoy failed to sway him.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says Taipei envoy failed to sway him.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said after talks with Taiwan's foreign minister on Wednesday he would stick by his decision to recognise Beijing but would maintain the best possible relations with Taipei.
"At the end of next year we will sever diplomatic relations with Taiwan," Mandela told a news conference after his meeting in Pretoria with Minister John Chang.
He said the decision had been agonising but he had had to make it in the interests of South Africa. "We are going to maintain relations from the highest level short of diplomatic relations."
Chang told reporters he understood the reasons behind Mandela's decision but hoped that relations would remain good.
"We believe we can work out a formula of future relations that will serve the interests of both sides," Chang said.
Mandela said a joint committee would work out details of the future relationship. On the possible negative impact on Taiwanese investment in South Africa, he said:
"Naturally this would be our concern but I have been happy with statements from Taipei where business people say this decision will not affect their business relations with us."
